items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: I heard Tricky Sam... I saw the trombone player, Tricky, was down there with a guy named Kenneth Roane.

ctx.x: 1924 I come to New York, that's my first time in New York - not to stay, but my first time in New York. But in two weeks time - in Harlem it was over a hundred clubs, you know. And I heard, that's where I heard Tricky Sam, the same trombone player that wrecked it, in little places. I even remember, I think I remember the name, it went Green Hornet or Green Dragon or somethin' like that, in Harlem around 30 somethin' street and Lenox Avenue, in that neighborhood. Anyway I may be not exact about the date, but he…
PS: Same guy who played with like among other bands, he played with a band from Springfield, Ohio, the Cecil Scott/Lloyd Scott -

items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: Besides Tricky Sam Nanton, what other people did you hear at that time that impressed you?

ctx.x: Still the afternoon of June the 6th, a Sunday in 1982. This is the beginning of our third reel on this particular afternoon, and I am Phil Schaap and this is the interview for the Jazz Oral History Project of Benny Waters, to be archived at the Institute of Jazz Studies, Rutgers University in Newark. Benny, we're gonna break away from the chronology in the second, or actually just leap forward in it to a different period. I want to ask you one last question about the 2 weeks you were in New York in '24. Besides…

Oh, I heard a band with a guy named Leonard Fields, saxophone player and I don't know exactly who was drumming [?] for them. The trumpet player was a guy who used to go around with Sugar Ray Robinson as a valet or something. He played like Louie Armstrong, he sounded like Louie Armstrong and he tried, you see. I can't think of his name now, he was playing just like Louie Armstrong, I mean copy, you know, see. He was really inspired and had that voice all the time, in the street. I just can't pin his name. Well…
